due_when.clears_when: a gateway journal read shows no Stopping/Started pairs for ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.timer over a 30-min window that spans two git-sync ticks, or the manager kills it as benign with a stated reason

origin.rerun: ops exec channel (Tier 2, via AM-OPS): ssh ubuntu@10.0.0.251 'journalctl -u ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.timer --since -30min --no-pager'

what: IB gateway VM: ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.timer and ict-ib-gateway-reset.timer are STOPPED and RESTARTED every ~5 min (journal 2026-11-12 07:16Z..08:31Z, 15 cycles, read via gateway-forensics #25178). The cadence matches the ict-git-sync tick, which most likely re-installs the units each pass. The watchdog still fires and probes healthy (action=none), so nothing is broken. But a timer restart every tick can reset its schedule, and it floods the journal. Find which job restarts them (install_systemd_units.sh or the gateway's git-sync hook) and make the re-install idempotent: skip the restart when the unit file is unchanged. Note: the row that expected the watchdog timer to read INACTIVE is wrong; it reads active+enabled.
